outputSchema.description:
A tool payload after the caller's `format` argument has been applied.

Which shape arrives depends on the REQUEST rather than the data, which is
why this is a type rather than three call sites deciding for themselves:
`format=json` sends the tool's own shape, `format=toon` sends a compact
string envelope, and a TOON conversion that fails falls back to JSON while
saying so. Untagged, so the derived schema is an `anyOf` over exactly
those three arms — schemars emits `anyOf` for an untagged enum, not
`oneOf`, so the schema does not itself assert the arms are mutually
exclusive. A client tells them apart by the keys: `toon` and `result` are
the envelope's, and they are fixed rather than per-tool for that reason.

The envelope keys are fixed (`toon`, `result`) rather than derived from a
per-tool `data_key`. A property name that changes per tool cannot be stated
in a schema, so the old `result_toon` / `recipes_toon` / `recipe_toon` /
`results_toon` spelling is gone — the key no longer carries information the
tool name already gives, and the contract is now expressible.

name: admin_impersonate_start
description: Admin support: act as one user, through this connection only, for up to an hour. From the next call on, this connection is offered and served exactly what that user's own assistant is (their data, their tools; for a human coach, the members who allowed it), plus `admin_impersonate_end`. List the tools again after it starts. Nothing that would outlive the session (a token, a key, a connection, a consent) can be created, exports are refused, and every call is on the admin audit trail naming you and the user.

user.description: The email or account id of the user to act as. Never another admin.

expires_at.description:
When the session stops acting as the user (RFC 3339): an hour after
it started, never renewed.

note.description:
What to do next: list the tools again, and end the session with

session_id.description: The support session's id, as the audit trail names it.

user_id.description: The account this connection now acts as.

name: calculate_daily_nutrition
description: Calculate daily calorie and macronutrient needs from biometrics and goals, carbohydrate from the day's training. For an athlete with a medical/PAR-Q flag on file it returns qualitative `guidance` and `figures_withheld` instead of any amount: their clinician sets those.

activity_level.description: sedentary, lightly_active, moderately_active, very_active or extra_active

training_intensity.description: easy (HR zones 1-2), moderate (3), hard (4) or very_hard (5+)

training_minutes.description: Training minutes that day, planned or done; omit both for a rest day

carbohydrate_load.description: The table row the day's training was read as.

carbs_g.description:
Daily carbohydrate, grams: the middle of `carbs_g_range`, the figure
the fat and percentages are worked from.

carbs_g_range.description:
The day's carbohydrate range, grams (low, high): the 2016 joint ACSM
table row the day's training falls in.

energy_from_macros_kcal.description:
Energy the protein, carbohydrate and fat add up to, kcal/day: equal to
`tdee` unless the day's training calls for more carbohydrate than it
leaves room for (above) or a light day leaves more than fat's ceiling
(below).

goal.description: The training goal the split was computed for.

FigureAuthority.description: Who sets the withheld figures instead of the platform.

oneOf.description:
Not stated: outside Dravr's own apps and channels the answer says
nothing about who sets this athlete's amounts.

FiguresWithheld.description:
The machine-readable statement that figures were withheld, and why.

Present means the answer carries no amount to eat or drink: no energy,
macronutrient, fluid, sodium or caffeine intake. What a finished session
cost (its calories burned) still describes the session and is not an
intake. Relay `note` rather than supplying a number of your own.

note.description: What to tell the athlete, in plain words.

reason.description:
`medical_flag`: a medical / PAR-Q flag is on file.
`external_transport`: withheld for every athlete outside Dravr's apps.

set_by.description: `clinician`: who sets these amounts; `not_stated` outside Dravr's apps.

TrainingDayLoad.description:
A training day's load, as a row of the daily carbohydrate table

The table is Thomas, Erdman & Burke (2016), from Burke et al. (2011).

oneOf.description:
"Extreme commitment (e.g., > 4-5 h/d mod-high intensity exercise)":
8-12 g/kg/d

WithheldFigures.description: A prescriptive nutrition answer without its figures.

figures_withheld.description: Why the amounts are absent and who sets them.

guidance.description: What to do instead, qualitatively — foods and timing, no amounts.

WithheldReason.description: Why an answer came back without its nutrition figures.

oneOf.description: A medical / PAR-Q flag is on the athlete's dossier.

Served outside Dravr's own apps and channels, where amounts are

anyOf.description: The figures, when the gate withholds none.

name: commitment_cancel
description: Retract a commitment the athlete no longer wants to be held to; it is never counted or reported. Use when they drop it or circumstances change (injury, travel, a plan revision). Retracting is not failing: never use it to record that they missed it.

Whether one was actually cancelled. False when nothing open matched,
which is a success: the athlete is not committed either way.

name: commitment_create
description: Record a commitment the athlete just made, to be checked against their real activity when the window closes. Call it ONLY once the athlete has agreed to a specific number of sessions by a specific day — if they only said 'ok' to your suggestion, or gave no count or no deadline, ask them to confirm both and call it on their answer. Not for your own plans or reminders.

due_date.description: Last day that counts, YYYY-MM-DD in the athlete's local calendar; for 'this week', the coming Sunday from the current-date anchor.

sport.description: Lowercase sport slug the sessions must match ('run', 'ride', 'swim'); omit to count any activity.

statement.description: The promise in the athlete's own terms (≤ 200 characters), e.g. 'three easy runs this week'.

commitment_id.description: The commitment the agent can later cancel or check against.

duplicate_of_open_commitment.description:
Whether an open commitment already covered this. A duplicate is
dropped rather than stacked, so the agent can say "already noted"
instead of promising a second check. Always the inverse of `recorded`;
both are on the wire because they answer different questions.

recorded.description:
Whether this call created it. False when an identical open commitment
already existed, which is a success — see
`duplicate_of_open_commitment`.

sessions.description: How many sessions the athlete committed to.

sport.description: The sport, when the commitment named one.

window_end.description: RFC 3339 timestamp the window closes at.

name: get_provider_roster
description: Read the roster of the coaching platform you coach on (Intervals.icu, TrainingPeaks) and where each athlete on it stands with your Dravr groups. Dravr members it names are listed by Dravr name with a `state`, such as `linked`, `proposed` (awaiting their confirmation in the app), `proposable` (link them with `propose_athlete_link`), `member_not_sharing` (they stopped sharing with you) or `member_own_connection` (no link needed: you reach their calendar through your own account). Every other athlete is only counted, by state and by your access on the platform; their names are never shown. `next_steps` says what linking them takes. provider.description: Coaching platform to read (`intervals_icu`, `trainingpeaks`); omit to read every one you connected.

ProviderRosterAccess.description: The caller's access to a roster athlete, as their platform reports it.

oneOf.description: The platform lets the caller coach the athlete.

The platform lets the caller follow the athlete: their data reads,
nothing is written.
The platform lists the athlete but gives the caller no access to them.
The platform did not say: read as neither coach nor follower.

ProviderRosterCount.description:
How many roster athletes, of those no Dravr member is named for, share
one state and access.

access.description: The caller's access to them on the platform.

state.description:
Their state: `not_in_your_groups` or `roster_email_missing`, or a
link's state when the group the link was made in is gone.

ProviderRosterMember.description: A Dravr member the roster names, and where they stand.

access.description: The caller's access to them on the platform.

group.description:
The group of the caller's the member is in, where a link to them is
made.

name.description: The member's Dravr display name, never the name the platform lists.

members.description: The Dravr members the roster names, by name.

others.description: Every other roster athlete, as counts by state and access.

provider.description: The platform, as the `provider` argument names it.

refusal.description:
Why the roster was not read, when it was not; nothing else is listed
then.

roster_size.description:
Athletes the roster lists, the caller's own account not among them;
absent when it was not read.

ProviderRosterRefusal.description:
Why a platform's roster was not read, in the refusal shape every tool
answers with.

reason.description: The reason a caller branches on.

ProviderRosterState.description: Where a roster athlete stands with the caller's groups and links.

oneOf.description:
Linked: the member's data on the platform reads through the caller's
account.
Linked, but the link reads nothing: see `not_reading_because`.
A link was proposed; the member has not confirmed it in the app yet.
The member reads the platform through another human coach's link.

The member already holds a link of the caller's for another roster
entry.
The member can be proposed a link with `propose_athlete_link`.

Dravr, so it binds no one yet.

The member stopped sharing with the caller in every group the caller

The platform gives the caller no access to the athlete, so no link is
proposed.

The athlete's roster email is no member's of a group the caller
coaches.

linked yet.

platforms.description:
Each coaching platform read: the one named, else every one the caller
connected.

outputSchema.description:
A tool payload after the caller's `format` argument has been applied.

Which shape arrives depends on the REQUEST rather than the data, which is
why this is a type rather than three call sites deciding for themselves:
`format=json` sends the tool's own shape, `format=toon` sends a compact
string envelope, and a TOON conversion that fails falls back to JSON while

per-tool `data_key`. A property name that changes per tool cannot be stated
in a schema, so the old `result_toon` / `recipes_toon` / `recipe_toon` /
`results_toon` spelling is gone — the key no longer carries information the
tool name already gives, and the contract is now expressible.
